paragraphs.text: Saul’s overthrow and death, 1Ch 10:1-7. The Philistines triumph over Saul, 1Ch 10:8-10. The kindness of Jabesh-gilead towards Saul and his sons: his sin, 1Ch 10:11-14.
Of this and the following verses till 1Ch 10:13, see my notes on 1Sa 31, where we have the same thing expressed almost in thee same words.
i.e. all his children, to wit, then present with him, namely,

as it is expressed, 1Sa 31:6. For it is evident that Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth were not slain. But nothing is more common in Scripture and all authors, than to understand all of a great and most considerable part.
which was beneath Mount Gilboa, where the fight was, 1Ch 10:1.
And his body severed from his head to the wall of Beth-shan, 1Sa 31:10.
To wit, every day till evening, after the manner of the Jewish fasts.
the sense is, Wonder not that Saul fell by the hands of the Philistines, who were armed against him by his own sin and by God’s vengeance for it.
against God’s express, and plain, and positive command; which is a great aggravation of any sin.
paragraphs.anchor: Against the word of the Lord

paragraphs.text: which also was contrary to a manifest command, Lev 19:31, and moreover, contrary to his own conscience, which was so fully convinced hereof, that he had endeavoured the utter extirpation of all such persons, in pursuance of God’s law. See 1Sa 28:9.
paragraphs.anchor: For asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit

paragraphs.text: concerning the event of the approaching battle.

He did so, but not in a right manner, not humbly and penitently, not diligently and importunately, not patiently and perseveringly; but when God would not answer him speedily, he gives it over, and goes from God to the devil. Compare 1Sa 14:18,19. Such an inconsiderable and trifling inquiry as Saul made, is justly accounted to be no inquiry at all; as they are said not to eat the Lord’s supper, 1Co 11:20, who did eat it in a sinful and irregular manner.
